correctness.rationale: From \(h=r+a+b\) and Gorenstein divisibility, \(x=h/a\) and \(y=h/b\) satisfy \(1=r/h+1/x+1/y\). Writing \(x=gu\), \(y=gv\) with \(\gcd(u,v)=1\) gives \(k=guv-u-v\), \(a=rv/k\), \(b=ru/k\), and the coprimalities \(\gcd(k,u)=\gcd(k,v)=1\) force \(k\mid r\). Setting \(A=gu-1\), \(B=gv-1\) gives exactly \(AB=gk+1\), the congruence/gcd conditions, and \((g-1)^2\le gk+1\) gives \(g\le k+2\). The converse reconstructs integral weights and the required divisibility. Applying the two-heavy Reid--Tai inequalities to \(x,y\) proves automatic canonicity and terminality iff \(y>2\) and \(x>3\), equivalent to \(B>1\), \(A>2\). The nonterminal cases \(y=2\) and \(x=3\) give exactly the divisor family plus \((r,r)\). An independent exact finite reconstruction through \(r=30\) matched the core parametrization, direct divisibility, age tests, and boundary set; this finite replay only corroborates the symbolic proof.

final_claim: For every \(r\ge2\), the Gorenstein members of \(\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\) are in bijection with finite divisor-core data \((k,g,A,B)\) satisfying \(k\mid r\), \(1\le g\le k+2\), \(AB=gk+1\), \(A\ge B\ge1\), \(A\equiv B\equiv-1\pmod g\), and \(\gcd(A+1,B+1)=g\), with the stated weight formulas. Every such member is canonical, terminal exactly when \(B>1\) and \(A>2\), and the canonical non-terminal Gorenstein boundary has exactly \(\tau(2r)+1\) members.
